title: Structured talk, then a synthesis alone
statement: Structure discussion: give thinking or writing time before calling on anyone, prefer a scripted argue-both-sides sequence to open debate, and have each student produce the final synthesis alone.
detail: Research for the Grade 9 lesson ideas found the strongest causal evidence on participation in a longitudinal study of cold-calling, where comfort participating rose in high-cold-call classes and was unchanged in low ones (Dallimore, Hertenstein & Platt 2013), and guidance for remote classes converging on think or write time before calling on anyone and tracking who has been called against the roster (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0249-g9-idea-research-full-files.qmd`). A synthesis of structured academic controversy, where students research a side, present it, argue the opposite side, drop advocacy and synthesize to consensus, found higher achievement and more higher-level reasoning than debate or individual work (Johnson & Johnson 2009) (the same file). A systematic review and a field study of over-reliance on AI dialogue found reduced engagement and worse unaided performance, which the file reads as an argument for a synthesis turn the student produces alone (the same file).
against: The cold-calling effect is quasi-experimental and comes from adult students, not remote ones, and the remote adaptations are practitioner guidance; the controversy synthesis covers its authors' own program, strong within it and less independently replicated outside it; and neither over-reliance study tests multi-agent debate, so the synthesis-alone turn rests on an inferred risk (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0249-g9-idea-research-full-files.qmd`).
